title: Existence of normalized finite-cover presentations of qcqs etale limit sites
statement: Let I be a small nonempty cofiltered category and D : I → Scheme a diagram of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with quasi-compact quasi-separated transition morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and [def-weil-size-convention]. There exists a Presentation D in the precise sense of [def-per-qcqs-etale-limit-presentation]: a strict equivalent system of the qcqs small etale categories, their finite-cover object-and-arrow colimit site with finite limits and the specified terminal objects, and normalized projection geometric morphisms with their restriction comparisons. No assertion of the topos universal property, factorization of points, conservativity or reindexing invariance is included.

source.place: Tags 09YL and 0A35; ILO XX 4.4, printed p.373 (literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, PDF p.379).

proof.text: Write $Q(T)$ for the full qcqs subcategory of the small etale site of a qcqs scheme $T$. Its arrows, including affine open covers, are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], every arrow between its objects is qcqs, and fibre products over its objects remain qcqs. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] restricts to finite limits and finite-limit-preserving pullback functors on $Q(T)$. The finite covers are closed under pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]; identities and finite composites cover by surjectivity. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings], every etale cover of an object of $Q(T)$ refines to a finite affine etale cover. Every etale object is covered by affine opens, which are qcqs. Hence the finite topology on $Q(T)$ is induced from the full small etale site. The fully faithful comparison [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence], with set coefficients, gives $\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{et}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(Q(T))$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact] identifies the scheme-induced direct image with precomposition by pullback; the restrictions just constructed therefore identify these morphisms with those of the small etale topoi. This proves all the stage-site assertions used below.

proof.text: Normalize the identity pullbacks and apply [lem-coef-pseudofunctor-split-family-strictification] with $J=I^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $H$ the constant empty category. Evaluation equivalences and their coherent comparisons replace the pullback pseudofunctor by a strict one. Transfer finite covers along evaluation: a finite family covers exactly when its evaluated family covers. Equivalences preserve finite limits, so the strict transitions retain Step 1's properties. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] to the evaluation equivalences with these induced topologies and set coefficients to identify the old and new sheaf topoi.

source.place: Strictification: categories.tex Tag 004A; comparison for equivalent sites with induced topologies.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites], stage coverings define the colimit site and the structure functors define projection geometric morphisms. For all finite limits, lift a finite diagram to a stage and take its limit there. Given a test object, move it to a common later stage. The Hom formula of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories](3) and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] identify maps to that proposed limit with compatible families of maps to the diagram. This proves its universal property and preservation by each structure functor. The same calculation for the empty diagram gives singleton Hom sets, so every image of $Y_i/Y_i$ is terminal.

theorem presentation_nonempty
    (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ (i j : I) (a : i ⟶ j), QuasiCompact (D.map a)]
    [∀ (i j : I) (a : i ⟶ j), QuasiSeparated (D.map a)] :
    Nonempty (Presentation D)

split_report.summary: A strictly smaller component of the existing seven-step argument, with its original generic inputs retained. No chapter or unit route is replaced.
split_report.edge_cases: Cofiltered means nonempty; empty schemes are allowed, with empty covering families and potentially empty conservative point family. Identity reindexing compares arbitrary strictifications. Scheme isomorphisms preserve qcqs. No affine-transition or limit-scheme hypothesis is introduced.
